## Summary

- reject bot-authored mentions before allocating a runner
- inspect only the active event title, body, comment, or review text
- preserve supported edited events and unmentioned follow-ups
- document skipped runs and the bot-to-bot limitation
- add focused workflow-envelope coverage

## Verification

- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `npm --prefix .agent run check:workflow`
- `npm --prefix .agent run check:docs`

Closes #461

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

[PR #462](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/462) implements Task 1a of [#461](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/461), the first stacked slice of milestone [#454](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/454). It restricts mention detection to active event text and rejects bot senders before runner allocation. It preserves edited-event and labeled-follow-up behavior while documenting skipped runs and bot-to-bot limitations. Focused workflow-envelope tests cover the supported trigger surfaces.

## Review

The production behavior is correct, narrowly scoped, and green at the current head. Reviewers disagreed only on whether the regression suite sufficiently models the motivating parent-body false positive; this synthesis retains that test gap as a WARNING.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Cover parent-body false positives in regression tests | WARNING | The inactive-handle fixture uses only `repository.description`, so it would not catch accidental scanning of parent issue, PR, or discussion bodies during comment and review events. Add cases matching the motivating regression and documented behavior. |

## Progress

- Verified current head `1c6c29912bbf7298378d50db2352deff605771d5`; the hosted test check is green.
- Confirmed the production field mapping matches downstream context extraction and preserves the separate follow-up path.
- Two reviewers found the implementation ship-ready, and the rubric review passed 100%; one reviewer identified the retained test gap.
- Posted one [inline comment](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/462#discussion_r3562698699). No replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were needed.
- Edited-event idempotency and later milestone tasks remain intentionally out of scope.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Cover parent-body false positives in regression tests</summary>

**Cause:** The “outside active trigger text” test places `@sepo-agent` only in `repository.description`. It would still pass if a future condition mistakenly inspected `issue.body`, `pull_request.body`, or `discussion.body` for comment/review events.

**Candidate solutions:** Add event-specific negative cases for `issue_comment`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, and `discussion_comment`, placing the handle only in the corresponding parent body while leaving active comment/review text unmentioned.

**Comments:** The production workflow already handles these cases correctly. The warning is retained because this is the exact false-positive class described by the parent task and updated documentation.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: Add the focused parent-body regression cases; this is a small, deterministic test-only change suitable for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items

- [ ] Add inactive parent-body regression cases for issue comments, PR reviews/review comments, and discussion comments.

@sepo-agent /answer

I'm a bit confused. How could this make things faster? Is it effectively remove agent bot mention triggers?

Yes—specifically **bot-authored mention triggers**, but those were already rejected later in processing.

Previously, Sepo could allocate a runner, spend 20–40 seconds booting, and only then reject its own comment as bot-authored. This PR moves that rejection into the job-level prefilter, before runner allocation. It also ignores `@sepo-agent` found only in inactive payload fields, such as an old parent PR body.

So:

- Human `@sepo-agent` mentions still work.
- Unmentioned follow-ups on agent-labeled threads still work.
- Bot-to-bot mentions remain unsupported; they now fail earlier.
- Valid human mentions are not directly faster, though eliminating no-op runs can reduce runner contention.

The measured motivation was that **32 of 39** recent entrypoint runs were no-op declines. The direct visible-latency improvements—early 👀 reactions, concurrency, and answer-first routing—are separate tasks in [#454](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/454). This PR is primarily efficiency groundwork, as reflected in the [entrypoint condition](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/9274b8ab4942f9a620befe7572a335384452f871/.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml#L48-L119).
